paper_metadata.title: Efficient Hamiltonian Simulation for Solving Option Price Dynamics

experiments.description: Digital quantum simulation of the Black-Scholes put-option PDE using Hamiltonian simulation with QFT-based diagonalization, unitary dilation with one ancilla qubit, and post-selection; evaluated via convergence against the analytical solution for multiple discretizations and via success-probability estimates.

algorithm.variant: Black-Scholes Hamiltonian simulation via Schrödinger mapping, QFT diagonalization, and unitary dilation post-selection
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state prepared from the duplicated European put payoff function.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Position space discretized on Nx = 2^n points; payoff encoded in amplitudes over duplicated basis states |x_j> and |x_{Nx-1-j}>; momentum space handled by QFT.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the Black-Scholes PDE by mapping it to ∂V/∂τ = i H_BS V with H_BS = i(σ^2/2)p^2 - (σ^2/2 - r)p + ir I, then recover the option price from the evolved state.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Periodic boundary conditions imposed through discretized momentum operator; initial condition duplicated by reflection to mitigate edge effects; post-selection on ancilla state |0_E>.

problem_instance.description: European put option pricing under constant volatility and interest rate, with numerical convergence studied across discretization sizes.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic Black-Scholes parameters; payoff V_p(T,S)=max(K-S,0); simulations shown for S_max=150, K=50, sigma=0.2, r=0.04, T=1 year.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Change of variables S = e^x; time reversal τ = T - t; discretization of x on an equispaced grid; payoff shifted and duplicated to enforce periodicity.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of numerical solution against analytical solution; convergence plot over n = 1..8 and discretization error per point over n = 1..9; success probability estimated analytically and lower-bounded.

hardware.framework: QFT-based digital quantum simulation; source code referenced on GitHub

implementation_details.classical_solver: Analytical Black-Scholes solution for validation; finite-difference discretization used for comparison in figures
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Analytical/numerical construction of payoff and discretized operators; duplication of initial condition.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Post-selection on ancilla |0_E>; measurement of position basis state via POVM and optional amplitude estimation for improved sampling.

speedup_claims.conditions: for expected-value estimation via amplitude estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a general amplitude-estimation claim cited in the paper, not specifically benchmarked on the Black-Scholes simulation circuit.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical PDE solvers such as Crank-Nicolson / FFT-based methods
speedup_claims.conditions: fault-tolerant quantum computer; QSP-based Hamiltonian simulation with QFT diagonalization
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quantum simulation is optimal for sparse Hamiltonians and gives asymptotic query complexity, but does not provide a direct end-to-end runtime comparison or crossover point.

speedup_claims.conditions: fault-tolerant quantum computer; one ancillary qubit plus discretization qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a resource estimate rather than a measured speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(td||H||_max + log(1/ϵ)/log log(1/ϵ)) oracle queries for QSP; QFT subroutine O(n log n)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(T_steps 2^n) for Crank-Nicolson; O((n+1)2^n) for FFT-based method; O(2^n) for matrix exponentiation
